rounds.text: Somany Ceramics Ltd is exhibiting an extraordinary acceleration in fundamental performance that is not yet fully reflected in traditional valuation multiples, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 85% [E21] and a massive net profit surge of 386% year-on-year [E67]. Operational efficiency is reaching elite levels, highlighted by a quarterly operating margin expanding by 4 percentage points to 12% in June 2026 [E31] and an impressive cash conversion ratio of 3.34x for March 2026, which proves that reported profits are overwhelmingly backed by actual cash [E34]. Furthermore, the company generated robust operating cash flow of Rs 247 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 197 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], comfortably positioning management to fund 65% to 70% of its upcoming capital expenditure through internal accruals [E93]. Growth catalysts are firmly in place through proactive capacity expansions, including a major upcoming greenfield plant in the South providing a revenue potential of about INR 350 crores [E83] alongside additional debottlenecking across existing lines [E84], while plants currently run at 100% capacity [E91]. Conceded: the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 2.98x against a sector benchmark of 2.01x [E7], and long-term historical sales growth has been modest at 5% over 10 years [E14].

Somany Ceramics carries severe valuation and structural risks that are flatly disconnected from the underlying business reality, starting with a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 363 against a market price of Rs 612, representing a negative margin of safety of 68.8% [E46, E47]. This rich valuation leaves the stock trading at 2.98 times its book value compared to a sector benchmark of 2.01x [E7], alongside an institutional money flow reading of negative 2.18 percentage points driven by domestic institutions cutting their stake from 23.65% to 19.42% [E44, E45]. Furthermore, long-term growth is remarkably muted, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 5% [E14], a 10-year profit growth of a meager 2% [E18], and a 5-year compounded share price growth of -6% [E23]. Operational headwinds compound these concerns, with borrowings increasing to Rs 374 Cr from Rs 360 Cr a year earlier [E40], and significant supply-side disruptions hitting the Morbi cluster due to elevated gas prices, fuel shortages, and labour unavailability [E96]. Conceded: the company recently posted strong TTM profit growth of 85% [E21], a quarterly operating margin expansion of 4 percentage points [E31], and healthy free cash flow of Rs 197 Cr [E36]. However, these short-term gains are heavily priced in by a reverse DCF implying an aggressive 11.2% earnings growth expectation [E48], while historical volatility remains high at 46.8% [E55] alongside a devastating worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -91.4% [E54].

Conceded: intrinsic value is modeled at Rs 363 by a DCF [E46, E47] and borrowings ticked up to Rs 374 Cr [E40]. However, the bear's fixation on stale 10-year growth figures completely misses the ongoing operational turnaround, which features an 85% surge in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E21] and a massive quarterly operating margin expansion to 12% in June 2026—a four percentage point jump over the prior-year quarter [E31]. The exit of domestic institutions [E44] ignores fundamental reality, as strong demand in May, June, and July has enabled the company to successfully pass on 16% to 18% gas price hikes [E80, E87]. Far from being overstretched, the business generated stellar free cash flow of Rs 197 Cr with profits fully backed by cash conversion of 3.34x [E34, E36], while running plants at 100% capacity [E91] and planning major greenfield expansion in the South to capture future housing demand [E83]. Conceded: historical volatility sits at 46.8% and past drawdowns are deep [E54, E55], but trailing operational momentum easily eclipses static long-term averages.

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 85% [E21] and June 2026 quarterly operating margins expanded by four percentage points [E31]. However, the bull's dismissal of long-term history glosses over a 10-year compounded profit growth rate of just 2% [E18] and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 11% [E15], confirming that the current surge follows a prolonged period of stagnation. The claim that institutional exits can be ignored [E44] disregards a negative money flow of 2.18 percentage points [E45], signaling persistent smart-money skepticism. Furthermore, while the bull celebrates 100% capacity utilization [E91], it ignores severe regional vulnerabilities, notably that Morbi exports are down 50% to 60% from their peak due to geopolitical headwinds [E95] alongside extreme natural gas price volatility [E87]. Conceded: free cash flow reached Rs 197 Cr [E36], but this strong cash generation is being immediately funneled into a heavy capital expenditure outlay of INR275 crores [E93], while borrowings have simultaneously ticked up to Rs 374 Cr [E40]. Finally, pointing to strong recent demand [E80] fails to justify a valuation where today's share price sits at 2.99x book value [E2]—substantially higher than the sector benchmark of 2.01x [E7]—leaving the stock dangerously exposed to its historical peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -91.4% [E54].

Conceded: 10-year compounded profit growth is 2% [E18] and 5-year compounded sales growth is 11% [E15]. However, looking backward ignores the current transformation where trailing twelve-month profit growth has surged by 85% [E21] and June 2026 quarterly operating margins expanded by 4 percentage points to 12% [E31]. Conceded: institutional money flow shows a negative change of 2.18 percentage points [E45], but this is easily absorbed by strong operational fundamentals and robust free cash flow of Rs 197 Cr [E36], which comfortably covers 65% to 70% of the upcoming INR275 crores capex outlay through internal accruals [E93]. While Morbi exports are down due to geopolitical headwinds [E95], the company is operating plants at 100% capacity [E91], actively passing on gas price increases between 16% and 18% [E87], and strategically expanding capacity in the South and existing lines [E83, E84] to capture sustained demand from housing, infrastructure, and renovation segments [E81]. Finally, the higher price-to-book ratio of 2.98x [E7] is justified by superior returns on capital, including an ROCE of 12.38% and an ROA of 5.02% that both outperform their sector benchmarks [E8, E10], alongside outstanding cash conversion of 3.34x backing reported profits [E34].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth has surged by 85% [E21] and June 2026 quarterly operating margins expanded by 4 percentage points to 12% [E31]. However, dismissing 10-year compounded profit growth of 2% [E18] and 5-year compounded sales growth of 11% [E15] ignores a multi-year history of stagnant compounding that invalidates short-term optimism. Conceded: free cash flow reached Rs 197 Cr [E36] and internal accruals will fund 65% to 70% of the upcoming INR275 crores capex outlay [E93], but total borrowings simultaneously rose to Rs 374 Cr [E40], revealing that capital expenditure still relies on expanding debt obligations. Conceded: the company operates plants at 100% capacity [E91] and passes on gas price increases [E87], but domestic institutions cut their holdings by 4.23 percentage points [E44] and institutional money flow reads negative [E45], signalling that professional investors are fleeing despite these operational metrics. Finally, while the bull defends the 2.98x price-to-book ratio [E7] using sector comparisons [E8, E10], a discounted cash flow model explicitly values intrinsic shares at Rs 363 against a market price of Rs 612 [E46], leaving a severe negative margin of safety of -68.8% [E47].

evidence.quote: And we maintain that the EBITDA margins delivered in this quarter would be maintained, and we are trying to better our EBITDA margins, which we have delivered in last quarter and on this quarter.

evidence.fact: The company expects mid-single-digit volume growth for the year.
evidence.quote: Mid-single digits.

evidence.fact: The company's guidance is to improve EBITDA margin by at least 1.5% or more.
evidence.quote: our guidance is to improve EBITDA margin from here by at least 1.5% or more.

evidence.fact: Demand in May and June was pretty decent, and July has also been acceptable despite rains in many parts of the country.
evidence.quote: Other than that, the demand of May and June has been pretty decent. July also has been not bad considering that there's been rains in many parts of the country.

evidence.fact: Management remains optimistic about industry growth prospects supported by sustained demand from housing, infrastructure, and renovation segments.
evidence.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the industry’s growth prospects, supported by sustained demand from housing, infrastructure, and renovation segments.

evidence.fact: Domestic demand saw a gradual improvement during January and February.
evidence.quote: the domestic demand saw a gradual improvement during January and Feb on account of increased domestic demand reducing the pressure on -- from reducing the pressure from exports.

evidence.fact: The company announced setting up a 9-plus million square meter plant in the South, which will be ready in the next 12 to 15 months and provide a potential revenue of about INR350 crores.
evidence.quote: Because of that, we have announced setting up a 9 million square meter plant -- 9-plus million square meter plant in the South, which would be up and ready by in the next 12 to 15 months. This would give us a potential revenue of about INR350 crores.

evidence.fact: The company is taking steps to augment further capacity by 4 million to 5 million in existing lines in Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, and the South, ready from mid-quarter 3 and complete in quarter 4.
evidence.quote: Other than that, we are taking many more steps, which are all work in progress to augment further capacity by about 4 million to 5 million in our existing lines in Bahadurgarh in -- which is in Haryana and in Gujarat and in Morbi and also in the South. All put together, we will be adding another 4 million to 5 million for the mid -- this will be ready from mid-quarter 3 and would be completely in place in quarter 4.

evidence.fact: The major capex plan for next year is the 9-plus million square meter plant in the South with an approximate outlay of INR220 crores.
evidence.quote: Yes, the major capex plan is the 9-plus million square meter plant in the South, which is approximately INR220 crores outlay, which is for next year.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins for the quarter increased by 3.6% to 11.6% due to operational efficiencies from capacity utilization and JV performances.
evidence.quote: As a result of capacity utilization, our EBITDA margins have gone up on operational efficiencies, both on capacity utilization in our plants and also on the JV performances. So EBITDA margins go up by 3.6% to 11.6% for the quarter.

evidence.fact: Gas prices have been volatile with small monthly increases, but the company has been able to pass on price increases between 16% and 18%.
evidence.quote: The gas price has been extremely volatile. I had mentioned that in the earnings call for the FY26, but the gas price since then has been extremely volatile. Every month, there have been a small increases in gas price. Fortunately, we've been able to pass on all the gas price increase until now. So the current price increase has been between 16% and 18%.

evidence.fact: The blended natural gas price is about INR68 in the North and in the mid-70s in the South and Morbi.
evidence.quote: Yes. So our blended price comes in at about INR68. And South, we're still buying partly in spot. So South is -- South and Morbi are pretty much at the same level, which is close to mid-70s. And in the North, it is slightly lower, which is around the INR68, INR69 level. This is for natural gas.

evidence.fact: Morbi operations have resumed 100% production using expensive gas supplied by GEL.
evidence.quote: Morbi operations have completely started. They have resumed 100% production on very expensive gas, which is on -- which is being supplied by GEL, formerly known as GSPCL.

evidence.quote: Capacity utilization was largely flat from approximately 80% to 79%. So that is largely flat.

evidence.quote: So we're running plant at 100% capacity.

evidence.quote: So all put together, we are at about INR275 crores, and we will be funding about 65%, 70% of this through internal accruals.

evidence.fact: Working capital was marginally lower by 4 days to 9 days.
evidence.quote: Working capital, we've done fairly well. It's marginally lower by 4 days to 9 days.
